easy.def: A Jewish religious leader.
examples: The rabbi gave a talk.
The rabbi is kind.
We met the rabbi.

more.def: A teacher and leader of the Jewish religion.
examples: The rabbi gave a talk at the synagogue.
The rabbi greeted every family.
We learned about the holiday from the rabbi.

easy.def: A small animal with long ears that hops.
examples: The rabbit hopped across the grass.
I feed my pet rabbit a carrot.
The rabbit has soft fur.

more.def: A small furry animal with long ears and a short tail that moves by hopping.
examples: The rabbit dug a burrow under the old tree.
Rabbits nibble on clover and lettuce.
A wild rabbit froze when it saw the fox.

easy.def: A contest to see who is fastest.
examples: We ran a race.
I won the race.
The race was fun.

more.def: A contest to see who can go the fastest or reach a place first.
examples: She won the race by one second.
The horses lined up for the big race.
Our class held a relay race on field day.

easy.def: To try to go the fastest.
examples: We race to the tree.
The cars raced.
She races her brother.

more.def: To compete to see who can go fastest or arrive first.
examples: The boys raced each other to the gate.
Sailboats raced across the bay.
I raced my sister up the stairs.

easy.def: A frame or shelf for holding things.
examples: The coats are on the rack.
I put my bike in the rack.
The rack is full.

more.def: A frame or stand with hooks or shelves that holds things.
examples: The coats hung on the rack by the door.
I locked my bike in the bike rack.
A rack of pies cooled in the window.

easy.def: A frame with strings for hitting a ball.
examples: I hit the ball with my racket.
The racket is light.
She holds a tennis racket.

more.def: A light frame with a net of strings and a handle that is used to hit a ball.
examples: I hit the ball with my tennis racket.
The racket has new strings.
He swung the racket hard.

easy.def: A very loud noise.
examples: The kids made a racket.
The racket woke me.
What a racket!

more.def: A loud, annoying noise.
examples: The kids made a racket in the hall.
The racket from the street woke me up.
The band made such a racket that we covered our ears.

easy.def: A machine that finds things by sending out waves.
examples: The radar showed the storm.
Planes use radar.
The radar found the plane.

more.def: A machine that uses radio waves to find where things are.
examples: The radar showed a storm coming.
Airplanes use radar to avoid hills.
The radar spotted the flock of birds.

easy.def: A machine that plays sounds sent through the air.
examples: Turn on the radio.
We listen to the radio in the car.
The radio plays music.

more.def: A device that receives sounds sent through the air, such as music and news.
examples: We listen to music on the radio in the car.
A weather report came over the radio.
Grandpa fixed the old radio.

easy.def: A piece of old cloth.
examples: Wipe it with a rag.
The rag is dirty.
I used a rag to clean.

more.def: A scrap of old cloth that is used for cleaning.
examples: Dad wiped the car with an old rag.
I cleaned the table with a wet rag.
The rag was stained with oil.

easy.def: Very strong anger.
examples: He shook with rage.
She was in a rage.
The rage passed.

more.def: A very strong, wild feeling of anger.
examples: He shook with rage when his toy broke.
The giant roared in a rage.
Her rage faded after she took a deep breath.

easy.def: To go into a place suddenly and take things.
examples: The bears raid the garbage.
The ants raided the pantry.
Raccoons raid the corn.

more.def: To enter a place suddenly to take something.
examples: The raccoons raided the trash cans at night.
The ants raided the pantry for sugar.
Hungry birds raid the berry bush.

easy.def: Tracks that trains run on.
examples: The railroad goes to the city.
We crossed the railroad.
The railroad is long.

more.def: A road made of steel rails on which trains travel.
examples: The railroad crosses the river on a bridge.
Workers built the railroad across the country.
We waited as the train rumbled along the railroad.

easy.def: Water that falls from the sky.
examples: Rain fell on the roof.
I love the sound of rain.
We played inside in the rain.

more.def: Drops of water that fall from clouds.
examples: Heavy rain filled the creek.
Rain tapped on the window.
We walked home in the rain.

easy.def: To fall as drops of water from the sky.
examples: It rains a lot here.
It rained all day.
I hope it does not rain.

more.def: To fall from the clouds in drops.
examples: It rained all afternoon, so we stayed in.
It rarely rains in the desert.
I hope it does not rain on the day of the picnic.

easy.def: Colors in the sky after rain.
examples: I saw a rainbow.
The rainbow has seven colors.
A rainbow came out after the rain.

more.def: An arch of many colors that you see in the sky when sun shines through rain.
examples: We saw a rainbow after the storm.
A rainbow has red, orange, yellow, green, blue and purple.
The rainbow stretched across the whole sky.

easy.def: To lift something up.
examples: Raise your hand.
They raised the flag.
He raised the box.

more.def: To lift something up to a higher place.
examples: Raise your hand if you know the answer.
The crew raised the flag.
She raised the window to let in air.

easy.def: To grow plants or care for animals or children.
examples: Farmers raise cows.
They raise chickens.
She raised a puppy.

more.def: To take care of a child or animal as it grows up, or to grow crops.
examples: Farmers in this valley raise sheep.
My grandparents raised four children.
She raised the puppy from the day it was born.

easy.def: To collect money.
examples: We raised money for the shelter.
The class raised fifty dollars.
They raise money for books.

more.def: To collect money for a purpose.
examples: The students raised money for the animal shelter.
Our town raised enough to build a new playground.
We raised a hundred dollars at the bake sale.

easy.def: A big meeting of people for a cause.
examples: We went to a rally.
The rally was loud.
The rally was in the park.

more.def: A large gathering of people who meet to support something.
examples: We went to a rally in the park.
Students held a rally to support the team.
The crowd cheered at the rally.

easy.def: A male sheep.
examples: The ram has horns.
A ram stood on the hill.
The ram is strong.

more.def: A male sheep, often with curved horns.
examples: The ram butted the fence with its horns.
A ram stood guard over the flock.
The ram has big, curly horns.

easy.def: To crash into something hard.
examples: The truck rammed the gate.
The boat rammed the dock.
He rammed his cart into the wall.

more.def: To hit something with great force.
examples: The boat rammed into the dock.
The truck rammed the fence.
He rammed the cart into the wall by accident.

easy.def: A big farm for raising cows or horses.
examples: The cowboy lives on a ranch.
The ranch has horses.
We visited a ranch.

more.def: A very large farm where cattle, horses or sheep are raised.
examples: The cowboys on the ranch ride horses every day.
The ranch had thousands of cows.
We spent a week at a ranch in Texas.

easy.def: By chance, with no plan.
examples: I picked a random card.
The prize went to a random winner.
A random number came up.

more.def: Chosen or done by chance, with no plan or pattern.
examples: I picked a random card from the deck.
The winner was chosen at random.
The teacher called on a random student.

easy.def: A line of mountains.
examples: We saw a mountain range.
Snow covers the range.
A long range is far away.

more.def: A group of mountains that are joined together in a long line.
examples: The Rocky Mountains are a long range in North America.
Clouds hung low over the mountain range.
The climbers crossed a high range to reach the valley.

easy.def: To go from one point to another.
examples: Prices range from one to five dollars.
The ages range from six to eight.
The colors range from pale blue to dark.

more.def: To stretch between two limits, from the smallest to the biggest.
examples: Temperatures here range from freezing in winter to hot in summer.
The students range in age from eight to ten.
The books on the shelf range from picture books to long novels.

easy.def: A person who takes care of a park.
examples: The ranger helped us.
A ranger watches the forest.
The park ranger showed us the map.

more.def: A person whose job is to look after a park or forest.
examples: The park ranger showed us the trail map.
A ranger watches the forest for fires.
The rangers counted the bears in the park.

easy.def: How high someone is in a group.
examples: The captain has a high rank.
What is her rank?
He rose in rank.

more.def: A person's level or position in a group such as an army.
examples: A captain has a higher rank than a sergeant.
He rose in rank after years of service.
The soldiers stood in ranks.

easy.def: To put in order from first to last.
examples: We rank the teams.
Our team ranked first.
The class ranked the books.

more.def: To place something in order from highest to lowest.
examples: The judges ranked the teams from best to worst.
Our school ranked first in the spelling contest.
I would rank her story at the top.

easy.def: To knock quickly on something.
examples: I rap on the door.
She rapped on the window.
He rapped the table.

more.def: To hit something quickly and lightly several times.
examples: She rapped on the door and waited.
He rapped on the window to get my attention.
The teacher rapped on the desk for quiet.

easy.def: A kind of music with words spoken in rhythm.
examples: I like rap.
The rap has a beat.
She wrote a rap.

more.def: A style of music in which words are spoken quickly in time with a beat.
examples: She wrote a rap about our school.
The rap had a strong beat.
The class made up a rap about the planets.

easy.def: Very fast.
examples: The cheetah is a rapid runner.
The hummingbird's wings are rapid.
He took rapid steps.

more.def: Very quick; happening in a short time.
examples: The river's rapid water carried the raft downstream.
The doctor felt the runner's rapid heartbeat.
The town has seen rapid growth in the last ten years.

easy.def: Very fast.
examples: The river flows rapidly.
The plant grew rapidly.
Her heart beat rapidly.

more.def: In a quick way, at high speed.
examples: The river flowed rapidly after the storm.
The weeds grew rapidly in the warm weather.
Her heart beat rapidly after the race.

easy.def: Not seen or found very much.
examples: It is rare to see snow here.
This is a rare stamp.
A rare bird came to our yard.

more.def: Not common; not often seen, found, or happening.
examples: The zoo has a rare white tiger.
Pandas are rare animals.
It is rare for him to be late.

easy.def: Not often.
examples: I rarely eat candy.
We rarely see snow.
She rarely misses school.

more.def: Not often, only on a few occasions.
examples: Snow rarely falls in the desert.
We rarely see snow in our town.
He rarely misses a day of school.

easy.def: Red spots on your skin that itch.
examples: I have a rash.
The rash itches.
The cream helped the rash.

more.def: A patch of red, itchy spots on the skin.
examples: I got a rash from the plant.
The cream made the rash go away.
He had a rash on his arm.

easy.def: Quick and not careful.
examples: It was a rash decision.
He made a rash choice.
The rash jump was risky.

more.def: Done in a hurry without thinking about what might happen.
examples: It was a rash decision to jump without looking.
He made a rash choice and lost his toy.
Do not be rash with your money.

easy.def: A small animal with a long tail, like a big mouse.
examples: A rat ran across the road.
The rat has a long tail.
Rats can swim.

more.def: A small furry animal with a pointed nose and a long tail, bigger than a mouse.
examples: A rat scurried along the wall.
Some people keep rats as pets.
Rats are good at finding their way through mazes.

easy.def: How fast something goes.
examples: The car moves at a fast rate.
The rate of growth.
The heart's rate.

more.def: How fast something happens or moves.
examples: The car traveled at a rate of sixty miles an hour.
Her heart rate rose when she ran.
Plants grow at different rates.

easy.def: A price for something.
examples: The rate is ten dollars.
The hotel rate.
A low rate.

more.def: The price charged for something, usually by the hour or day.
examples: The hotel's rate is ninety dollars a night.
The rate for the bike was five dollars an hour.
We got a low rate for the cabin.

easy.def: A little bit.
examples: It is rather cold.
She was rather sad.
The test was rather hard.

more.def: To some degree; fairly.
examples: It was rather cold, so we wore our coats.
The box was rather heavy for a small child.
He was rather tired after the long hike.

easy.def: Used to show that you like one thing better.
examples: I would rather play outside.
She would rather have tea.
I would rather read.

more.def: Used to say that you like one choice more than another.
examples: I would rather walk than ride the bus.
She would rather have juice than milk.
Would you rather swim or fish?

easy.def: A score or grade that shows how good something is.
examples: The movie has a good rating.
The restaurant's rating is high.
The rating is four stars.

more.def: A score or level that shows how good or bad something is.
examples: The hotel received a high rating from guests.
The restaurant's rating is four stars.
The game's rating shows it is for all ages.

easy.def: To make short, quick, knocking sounds.
examples: The window rattled.
The coins rattle.
The wind rattles the door.

more.def: To make a quick series of sharp sounds, or to shake something so that it makes them.
examples: The windows rattled in the wind.
The coins rattled in the jar.
The old truck rattled down the road.

easy.def: A baby toy that makes noise.
examples: The baby shakes a rattle.
The rattle is noisy.
The rattle is blue.

more.def: A baby's toy, or the tail part of a snake, that makes a quick shaking noise.
examples: The baby shook her rattle.
The rattle of a snake warns other animals.
The rattle made a loud noise.

easy.def: Not cooked.
examples: The carrot is raw.
Do not eat raw eggs.
I like raw vegetables.

more.def: Not cooked, or in its natural state before being made into something.
examples: I like to eat raw carrots.
Raw chicken must be cooked well.
The factory uses raw cotton to make cloth.

easy.def: A tool with a sharp blade for shaving.
examples: Dad shaves with a razor.
The razor is sharp.
Do not touch the razor.

more.def: A tool with a very sharp blade, used to shave hair from the skin.
examples: Dad shaved his face with a razor.
The razor is very sharp, so do not touch it.
He put a new blade in the razor.
